items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: Interviewer asks about Lorenzo Flournoy; Interviewee confirms he had a band/trio and played piano, but does not describe a direct personal or professional interaction with Flournoy himself.

ctx.x: And another time that I worked with Hazel, they did another movie, it was something about -- they did a tune for her, "when the black keys meet the white keys ..." and something; right now, that particular type of song would be termed as corny, but I can't remember all those movies, really, but I did an awful lot of movies. Awful lot of movies.
Lorenzo Flournoy is a name that keeps coming up. Did he have a band or a trio or what? I know he had a trio in later years.

Yeah, well he did have a trio later, but at first, he used to have a band at the Alabam; he had about 8 pieces, and Doetsie Williams was in it, and there was a very good drummer here in town that he and I were really, really competitors, because we were around the same age -- I think he may have been 2 or 3 years older than I was. His name was Oscar Bradley, and the guy was really -- he was a good drummer. We had different styles. I patterned myself kind of at the time, as I told you, about the drummer with Buck…
